text:
vivian: Heads-up — after I pushed the RBAC shrink for ns=onprem-keystore, we're seeing outbound TLS to 198.51.100.77 (unapproved) from keystore-sidecar on node build-node-3. Not sure if it's DNS, a bootstrap script, or a leaked token. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: [ALERT] onprem cluster egress anomaly 2026-11-08T09:43Z. 29 connections to 198.51.100.77 from svcaccount:keystore-sidecar.

anita: Oncall. Please paste the exact kubectl patch + which pods/nodes are affected. Also run `kubectl get pods -n onprem-keystore -o wide -l app=keystore` and `kubectl logs -n onprem-keystore keystore-sidecar-*-container --since=15m`.

vivian: Patch was a namespace rolebinding reduction: `kubectl patch rolebinding onprem-keystore-secrets -n onprem-keystore --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/roleRef/name","value":"keystore-read"}]'` applied at 09:41:12Z. Affected pods: keystore-0 (node build-node-3) and keystore-1 (node db-node-2).

dinesh: VPC/edge logs show egress from build-node-3 at 09:41:40. Interesting detail: build-node-3 had a recent config drift fix from the CI pipeline; CI pipeline logged an ssh-based bootstrap step at 09:30 that modified /etc/hosts on multiple builder nodes. Can someone check node /etc/hosts and systemd unit logs?

kevin: I can ssh into build-node-3. Found hosts override: `198.51.100.77 kms.internal # added by ci-bootstrap-2026-11-08` — looks like the pipeline added this while patching some image layers. Also the keystore sidecar init container uses the node-local resolver for its startup probe (nsswitch order), so it picked the poisoned host for initial health checks and later for requests.

anita: That explains it. Containment: 1) rotate SA tokens for keystore sidecar 2) remove hosts override on build-node-3 and any other nodes the bootstrap touched 3) patch affected Deployments to temp-noegress SA and restart pods 4) apply network-level deny for 198.51.100.77 at the egress gateway until we verify.

ops-bot: Suggested commands:
```
# remove hosts entry on node (run via ops runbook)
sudo sed -i '/kms.internal/d' /etc/hosts
# rotate token
kubectl delete secret -n onprem-keystore sa-keystore-sidecar-token-*
# patch deployment to temp-sa
kubectl create sa temp-noegress -n onprem-keystore || true
kubectl patch deploy keystore -n onprem-keystore -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"temp-noegress"}}}}'
```

ci-pipeline-bot: Pipeline record: job/infra/ci-bootstrap ran at 2026-11-08T09:29:12Z and executed script `scripts/bootstrap-hosts.sh` which contains `echo "198.51.100.77 kms.internal" >> /etc/hosts` under the legacy image-fix step. It was merged in the hotfix MR #7893.

vivian: Ugh — MR slipped. We need to audit the pipeline and gate any host file edits. Forensics: capture node disk and pod fs snapshot, collect kube-apiserver audit and sidecar logs.

security-bot: Quick lookup: 198.51.100.77 resolves to kms-legacy-outside.example.net (external). Recommend immediate egress deny and revocation of any grants to that host. Also flag the CI job author for review.

dinesh: Collected artifacts: /etc/hosts snapshot from build-node-3, init container logs showing DNS resolution to 198.51.100.77 at 09:40:58, kube-audit slice 09:35-09:50. Audit shows repeated GET /v1/decrypt calls from `system:serviceaccount:onprem-keystore:keystore-sidecar` between 09:41:00-09:41:36. No impersonation entries.

anita: Action owners: kevin — remove hosts entry + remediate other nodes; vivian — open vuln-triage/inc ticket and contact compliance/legal if external decrypts confirmed; dinesh — collect full forensic tarball and run image scan `trivy` on the sidecar image. I'll own RBAC rollback mitigations and runbook updates.

kevin: Remediated hosts on build-node-3 and build-node-4 (both had the same bootstrap step). Rotated tokens, restarted pods against temp-noegress SA, and applied egress deny at edge for 198.51.100.77. Monitoring reports no further egress.

vivian: Created ticket INC-2026-1144 and uploaded artifacts: hosts snapshots, audit slice, pod logs, and pipeline job log. Looping in legal and product-security.

dinesh: For triage I'm running `trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL keystore-sidecar:sha256-abcd` and preserving node disk images. Early scan found no plaintext secrets in image layers. Will follow up with deeper forensic.

anita: Postmortem action items (short list): 1) ban direct /etc/hosts edits in CI; require DNS change requests through infra pipeline with review 2) make preflight probes validate resolved IP against allowlist and TLS SAN 3) gate RBAC changes touching secrets with an egress smoke test 4) enforce short TTLs for SA tokens and automated rotation 5) add alerting for external KMS-host hits from onprem clusters.

vivian: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the incident anchor — will post timeline and RCA once forensic analysis completes. :white_check_mark:
